title: Road Repairs
statementMd:
A country named Berland has $n$ cities. They are numbered with integers from $1$ to $n$. The city with index $1$ is the capital of the country. Some pairs of cities have monodirectional roads built between them. However, not all of them are in good condition. For each road, we know whether it needs repairing or not. If a road needs repairing, then it is forbidden to use it. However, the Berland government can repair the road so that it can be used.

Right now, Berland is being threatened by the war with the neighbouring state. So the capital officials decided to send a military squad to each city. The squads can move only along the existing roads, as there's no time or money to build new roads. However, some roads will probably have to be repaired in order to get to some cities.

Of course, the country needs a lot of resources to defeat the enemy, so you want to be careful with what you prioritize. That's why the Berland government wants to repair the minimum number of roads that is enough for the military troops to get to any city from the capital, driving along good or repaired roads. Your task is to help the Berland government and to find out which roads need to be repaired.

## Input

The first line contains two space-separated integers $n$ and $m$ $(1 \le n, m \le 10^5)$ — the number of cities and the number of roads in Berland.

Next $m$ lines contain three space-separated integers $a_i, b_i, c_i$ $(1 \le a_i, b_i \le n, a_i \ne b_i, 0 \le c_i \le 1)$, describing the road from city $a_i$ to city $b_i$. If $c_i$ equals $0$, then the given road is in good condition. If $c_i$ equals $1$, then it needs to be repaired.

It is guaranteed that there is at most one road between the cities in each direction.

## Output

If even after all roads are repaired, it is still impossible to get to some city from the capital, print $-1$. Otherwise, on the first line print the minimum number of roads that need to be repaired, and on the second line print the numbers of these roads, separated by single spaces.

The roads are numbered starting from $1$ in the order in which they are given in the input.

If there are multiple sets consisting of the minimum number of roads to repair to make travelling to any city from the capital possible, print any of them.

If it is possible to reach any city, driving along the roads that already are in good condition, print $0$ in the only output line.
statementZhMd:
一个名为 Berland 的国家有 $n$ 座城市，编号为 $1$ 到 $n$。编号为 $1$ 的城市是该国的首都。部分城市对之间修建了单向道路。但并非所有道路的状况都良好。对于每条道路，我们都知道它是否需要维修。如果一条道路需要维修，则禁止使用它。不过，Berland 政府可以维修这条道路，使其能够通行。

目前，Berland 正受到邻国的战争威胁。因此，首都的官员决定向每座城市派遣一支军队。由于没有时间或资金修建新道路，这些军队只能沿现有道路移动。不过，为了到达某些城市，可能必须维修一些道路。

当然，国家需要大量资源来击败敌人，因此你希望谨慎安排优先级。为此，Berland 政府希望维修数量最少的道路，使军队能够从首都沿状况良好或已经修复的道路到达任意城市。你的任务是帮助 Berland 政府找出需要维修的道路。

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个用空格分隔的整数 $n$ 和 $m$ $(1 \le n, m \le 10^5)$，分别表示 Berland 的城市数量和道路数量。

接下来的 $m$ 行每行包含三个用空格分隔的整数 $a_i$、$b_i$、$c_i$ $(1 \le a_i, b_i \le n, a_i \ne b_i, 0 \le c_i \le 1)$，表示一条从城市 $a_i$ 通往城市 $b_i$ 的道路。如果 $c_i$ 等于 $0$，则给出的道路状况良好。如果 $c_i$ 等于 $1$，则这条道路需要维修。

保证每个方向的城市之间至多有一条道路。

## 输出格式

如果即使维修所有道路，仍然无法从首都到达某些城市，则输出 $-1$。否则，第一行输出需要维修的道路的最少数量，第二行输出这些道路的编号，编号之间用单个空格分隔。

道路按照它们在输入中出现的顺序从 $1$ 开始编号。

如果有多组需要维修的道路数量最少，且维修后可以从首都到达任意城市，输出其中任意一组。

如果只沿着原本状况良好的道路就可以到达任意城市，则只输出一行 $0$。
